title: Perfectness and cobase stability of coherent right-cone equivalences
statement: Use simplicial sets, internal functor simplicial sets and weak homotopy equivalences of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], and the coherent realization $\mathfrak C$ of [lem-coef-pinched-cube-latching]. For a small simplicial category $A$, write $\pi_0A$ for the category with the same objects and the path components of its mapping simplicial sets as morphisms. Call $u:U\to V$ a categorical equivalence when $\mathfrak C[u]$ induces weak homotopy equivalences on all mapping simplicial sets and an equivalence of the categories $\pi_0\mathfrak C[U]\to\pi_0\mathfrak C[V]$. Fix a small simplicial set $S$ in a universe enlarged if necessary. For $a:X\to S$, put $C_S(a)=S\amalg_X(X\star\Delta^0)$, where $(X\star\Delta^0)_r=X_r\amalg\{v_r\}\amalg\coprod_{0\leq u<r}X_u$ has the ordered-concatenation operators: a simplex in $X_u$ has its first $u+1$ vertices in $X$ and the remaining vertices at $v$, and restriction or repetition of vertices uses the corresponding operator on the surviving $X$ block, with an empty $X$ block giving $v_r$; a map $f:(X,a)\to(Y,b)$ over $S$ induces $C_S(f):C_S(a)\to C_S(b)$. Let $W_S$ be the class of maps $f$ over $S$ for which $C_S(f)$ is a categorical equivalence. Then $W_S$ contains all isomorphisms and satisfies two-out-of-three. It is closed under small filtered colimits in the arrow category of $\mathrm{sSet}_{/S}$, and there is a small set $W_{S,0}\subseteq W_S$ such that every member of $W_S$ is isomorphic to a small filtered colimit of members of $W_{S,0}$. Here filtered means that every finite diagram, including the empty one, has a cocone; arrows in the arrow category are commuting squares and colimits are computed on both endpoints. Moreover, in a pushout square $X\xrightarrow{f}Y$, $X\xrightarrow{i}X'$, $Y\to Y'$, $X'\xrightarrow{f'}Y'$ over $S$, if $f\in W_S$ and $i$ is degreewise injective, then $f'\in W_S$. These assertions hold in each input universe. No quasicategory hypothesis on $S$ is imposed.

source.place: Proof of Proposition 2.1.4.7, conditions (1) and (2), dualized by Remark 2.1.4.12; perfect inverse-image input Corollary A.2.6.14 and coherent-realization cofibration input in Theorem 2.2.5.1. No model existence or fibrancy assertion is included. No Stacks tag states this simplicial cone result. HTT read online, archival copy WANTED. Cone construction: Definition 2.1.4.2, right-cone clause. Expanded perfectness clauses: Definition A.2.6.12.

proof.text: Put $O=S_0\amalg\{v\}$ and $\mathcal A=\mathrm{sSet}_{/S}$, $\mathcal B=\mathrm{sCat}_O$. The category $\Delta/S$ is small: its objects are simplices $\sigma:\Delta^n\to S$, and its arrows $\sigma\to\tau$ are monotone maps $\alpha:[n]\to[m]$ with $\sigma=\tau\alpha$. The assignment $(X\to S)\mapsto((n,\sigma)\mapsto\{x\in X_n:a(x)=\sigma\})$ identifies $\mathcal A$ with set-valued presheaves on $\Delta/S$; its inverse takes the disjoint union of these fibers over each $S_n$. Thus [lem-coef-presheaf-local-presentability] makes $\mathcal A$ locally presentable. Colimits in the slice are underlying simplicial-set colimits with the induced map to $S$; pullbacks of a cospan over $S$ are underlying simplicial-set pullbacks with the induced map to $S$. For $\mathcal B$ use the small finite-limit sketch with sorts $B_n(x,y)$ for $n\geq0$, $x,y\in O$, face/degeneracy operations, identity constants and binary composition operations on $B_n(x,y)\times B_n(y,z)$, imposing the simplicial, associativity, unit and compatibility equations. It has exactly simplicial categories with object set $O$ as models. Apply [lem-coef-finite-limit-model-presentability]: $\mathcal B$ is locally presentable, complete and cocomplete, and its filtered colimits are computed on each mapping simplicial set. Both arrow categories are locally presentable by [lem-coef-presheaf-local-presentability] with index $[1]^{\mathrm{op}}$, since both endpoint categories have pullbacks. Their colimits are computed at the endpoints, as is checked by applying the colimit universal property to a commuting square. The operations in the sketch are finitary and its sorts form a small set; all these assertions therefore hold relative to the chosen input universe.

source.place: Proposition 2.1.4.7 setup; Appendix A.3.2; presentability inputs are the cited existing presheaf and finite-limit-model theorems.

proof.text: Define $F:\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$ by $F(a)=\mathfrak C[C_S(a)]$. The cone formula gives, in every degree $r$, the disjoint union $C_S(a)_r=S_r\amalg\{v_r\}\amalg\coprod_{0\leq u<r}X_u$: only the pure $X_r$ summand is glued to $S_r$. Each induced map is the identity on $S_r$ and $v_r$ and is $f_u$ on the mixed summand indexed by $u$. In particular every cone has exactly vertex set $O$ and every cone map fixes it. This formula preserves every small connected colimit: the constant summands have connected indexing category, while the other summands are evaluated colimits of $X_u$; these identifications commute with every simplicial operator by its ordered-block formula. Hence $C_S$ preserves filtered colimits and pushouts. To check the required colimit property of $\mathfrak C$, define $N(A)_n=\operatorname{Fun}_{\mathrm{sCat}}(\mathfrak C[\Delta^n],A)$ with restriction along monotone maps. By the defining simplex colimit in [lem-coef-pinched-cube-latching], a functor $\mathfrak C[K]\to A$ is exactly a compatible family indexed by simplices of $K$, equivalently a simplicial map $K\to N(A)$. For any colimit diagram in $K$, this description identifies maps out of $\mathfrak C[\operatorname{colim}K]$ with compatible maps out of its terms; it proves preservation of colimits. For a connected diagram of simplicial categories whose object maps are all the identity on $O$, the colimit in $\mathrm{sCat}$ has object set $O$ and is the colimit in $\mathrm{sCat}_O$: a compatible family to any simplicial category chooses one common object function from $O$, and its remaining data are precisely compatible maps on the enriched homs. Thus $F$ preserves filtered colimits and pushouts in $\mathcal B$.

source.place: Definition 2.1.4.2 and Proposition 2.1.4.7(1)-(2), right-cone version; the displayed summand and Hom calculations expand colimit preservation directly.

proof.text: For any $g:A\to B$ in $\mathcal B$, the identity on objects makes essential surjectivity of $\pi_0g$ automatic; if all mapping-set maps are weak homotopy equivalences, they induce bijections on path components, so $\pi_0g$ is also fully faithful. Consequently $g$ is a Dwyer--Kan equivalence exactly when it is a weak equivalence of the fixed-object model structure of [lem-coef-simplicial-interval-lifting]. Thus $f\in W_S$ exactly when every $F(f)(x,y)$ is a weak homotopy equivalence. Isomorphisms and two-out-of-three now follow on every mapping simplicial set from the Kan model structure of [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper], using $F(gf)=F(g)F(f)$. In particular this class is replete in the arrow category.

source.place: Proposition 2.1.4.7(1); Definition A.2.6.12(1)-(2), specialized to a common object set.

proof.text: Let $I$ be any small filtered category and let $f_i$ be an $I$-diagram of arrows in $W_S$. Step 2 identifies $F(\operatorname{colim}_I f_i)$ with $\operatorname{colim}_I F(f_i)$ in the arrow category of $\mathcal B$. By the finite-limit-model theorem in Step 1 this last colimit is computed separately on every $B(x,y)$; this uses filteredness, not arbitrary mappingwise computation of enriched pushouts. The statement [lem-coef-filtered-colimit-weak-equivalences] applies to those diagrams of mapping simplicial sets, with no injectivity condition on their transitions. Every resulting mapping-set map is therefore a weak homotopy equivalence. Step 3 gives $\operatorname{colim}_I f_i\in W_S$.

source.place: Proposition 2.1.4.7(1), Definition A.2.6.12(3), with filtered closure proved mappingwise; arbitrary filtered index categories are allowed.

proof.text: By [lem-coef-cone-sorted-theory-identification], the category $\mathcal B=\mathrm{sCat}_O$ is equivalent to strict simplicial algebras for the small $O\times O$-sorted theory $T_O$, with sort evaluation identified with $A\mapsto A(x,y)$. Apply [lem-coef-sorted-simplicial-algebra-model] to this theory. Its weak equivalences and fibrations are therefore exactly those of the fixed-object model used in Step 3; the two model structures also have the same cofibrations, since those are determined by lifting against trivial fibrations.

source.place: Example 3.5, Definition 3.6 and Theorem 4.7, printed pp.1937-1938,1942-1943; fixed-object specialization in the returned Step 5.

proof.text: Use the free mapping-set functor $L_{xy}$ of [lem-coef-fixed-object-free-arrow-adjunction], including $x=y$. Under Step 5 it is the free algebra functor, since both are left adjoint to the same evaluation. By [lem-coef-sorted-simplicial-algebra-model], $I_O=\{L_{xy}(\partial\Delta^n)\to L_{xy}(\Delta^n)\}$ and $J_O=\{L_{xy}(\Lambda_i^n)\to L_{xy}(\Delta^n)\}$ generate the fixed-object trivial fibrations and fibrations. The free/evaluation adjunction identifies each lifting square and its fillers with the corresponding simplicial-set square. [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper] thus identifies $I_O^{\square}$ as the mappingwise trivial Kan fibrations and $J_O^{\square}$ as the mappingwise Kan fibrations. Both families are small, indexed by $O^2$, $n\geq0$ for boundaries and $n\geq1$, $0\leq i\leq n$ for horns; the zero-dimensional boundary is retained.

source.place: Corollary A.2.6.8, proof of accessibility by the second-factor functor, expanded from Proposition A.1.2.5; Appendix A.3.2 fixed-object model. This is the accessibility input to A.2.6.14, not the slice-model existence theorem.

proof.text: Apply the accessible small-object factorization theorem to $J_O$ in the locally presentable category $\mathcal B$. It gives, functorially for every $g$, a factorization $g=p_g i_g$ with $p_g\in J_O^{\square}$, with $i_g$ in the weakly saturated class generated by $J_O$, and with a middle-object functor $E$ preserving $\kappa$-filtered colimits for some infinite regular $\kappa$.

source.place: Corollary A.2.6.8, proof of accessibility by the second-factor functor, expanded from Proposition A.1.2.5; Appendix A.3.2 fixed-object model. This is the accessibility input to A.2.6.14, not the slice-model existence theorem.

proof.text: In the Step 5 model, trivial cofibrations are the left lifting class ${}^{\square}(J_O^{\square})$. By [lem-coef-lifting-class-closure] it is closed under pushouts and arrow retracts, and by [lem-coef-transfinite-left-lifting] under small continuous transfinite compositions. It contains every isomorphism: in a square with invertible left side $j$ and top map $u$, the filler is $u j^{-1}$. Since it contains $J_O$, the defining minimality of weak saturation puts the weak saturation of $J_O$ inside it. Step 7 places $i_g$ in that weak saturation, so $i_g$ is a trivial cofibration.

source.place: Corollary A.2.6.8, proof of accessibility by the second-factor functor, expanded from Proposition A.1.2.5; Appendix A.3.2 fixed-object model. This is the accessibility input to A.2.6.14, not the slice-model existence theorem.

proof.text: Define $T(g)=p_g:E(g)\to\operatorname{target}(g)$ and $T(a,b)=(E(a,b),b)$. The naturality equation $p_hE(a,b)=bp_g$ from [lem-coef-accessible-small-object-factorization] is exactly the required commuting square. Its identity and composition compatibility makes $T$ a functor.

source.place: Corollary A.2.6.8, proof of accessibility by the second-factor functor, expanded from Proposition A.1.2.5; Appendix A.3.2 fixed-object model. This is the accessibility input to A.2.6.14, not the slice-model existence theorem.

proof.text: For a small $\kappa$-filtered diagram of arrows $g_d$, the comparison $\operatorname{colim}_d T(g_d)\to T(\operatorname{colim}_d g_d)$ has source component $\operatorname{colim}_d E(g_d)\to E(\operatorname{colim}_d g_d)$, an isomorphism by [lem-coef-accessible-small-object-factorization], and target component the identity of $\operatorname{colim}_d\operatorname{target}(g_d)$. Arrow colimits are endpointwise by the same cited statement; the comparison is a square by naturality of $p$. A square whose two components are invertible is inverted componentwise. Hence $T$ preserves these colimits.

source.place: Corollary A.2.6.8, proof of accessibility by the second-factor functor, expanded from Proposition A.1.2.5; Appendix A.3.2 fixed-object model. This is the accessibility input to A.2.6.14, not the slice-model existence theorem.

proof.text: By [lem-coef-small-right-lifting-accessibility], the replete full subcategory $R\subseteq\mathcal B^{[1]}$ of maps with the right lifting property against $I_O$ is accessible. Put $H=T\circ F^{[1]}:\mathcal A^{[1]}\to\mathcal B^{[1]}$, where $F^{[1]}$ applies $F$ at both endpoints of an arrow and both sides of a square. Steps 2 and 10 show that $H$ preserves $\kappa$-filtered colimits. For each $f$, the first factor $i_{F(f)}$ is a weak equivalence, so two-out-of-three in the fixed-object model gives $F(f)$ weak equivalent if and only if $p_{F(f)}$ is weak equivalent. The latter map is already a fibration; therefore it is a weak equivalence if and only if it is an $I_O$-injective, by the two generating families in Step 6. We have proved the equality of full subcategories $W_S=H^{-1}R$. Apply [lem-coef-accessible-full-inverse-image] to the locally presentable arrow categories from Step 1, the functor $H$ and the replete accessible subcategory $R$. It supplies an infinite regular $\lambda$ and a small family $W_{S,0}\subseteq W_S$ generating $W_S$ under small $\lambda$-filtered colimits in the ambient arrow category. Every $\lambda$-filtered category is filtered since $\lambda$ is infinite, so this is the required small filtered-colimit generating family. Its cardinal need not be the factorization cardinal. Along with Steps 3 and 4 this proves every stated perfectness clause in the input universe.

source.place: Corollaries A.2.6.7 and A.2.6.8, proof, and Corollary A.2.6.14; Definition A.2.6.12(4). The full inverse-image result applies to the second-factor functor on arrow categories, not just a functor induced on endpoints.

proof.text: Let $i:(X,a)\to(X',a')$ be degreewise injective over $S$. In the disjoint-union formula of Step 2, $C_S(i)$ is the identity on the pure $S_r$ and apex summands and equals $i_u$ on each mixed summand. Therefore it is degreewise injective, including degree zero where it is the identity on $O$. Apply [lem-coef-coherent-fixed-vertex-cofibrations] to $C_S(i)$. It follows that $F(i)$ is a cofibration in $\mathcal B=\mathrm{sCat}_O$; all its objects are the fixed vertices, even if $X$ is empty or its structure map identifies vertices in $S$.

source.place: Proposition 2.1.4.7(2), using only the initial boundary-cube cofibration calculation in the proof of Theorem 2.2.5.1, printed p. 90.

proof.text: Apply $F$ to the pushout square of the statement. By Step 2 it is a pushout square in $\mathcal B$, not merely a square of underlying graphs. Since $f\in W_S$, Step 3 makes $F(f)$ an objectwise weak homotopy equivalence; Step 12 makes $F(i)$ a fixed-object cofibration. The statement [lem-coef-fixed-object-scat-left-proper] applies to exactly these hypotheses, without local Kan assumptions, and says that $F(f'):F(X')\to F(Y')$ is an objectwise weak homotopy equivalence. Step 3 translates this back to $f'\in W_S$. The proof used no horn filling assumption on $S$ and all the signatures, indexing categories and generating families used above are small in the chosen universe, proving the arbitrary-base and universe clauses as well.

source.place: Proposition 2.1.4.7(2), right-cone argument corresponding to Remark 2.1.4.12; use the existing fixed-object left properness theorem directly.
